title: Predictive headroom reservation and adaptive KV/activation budgeting
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Production inference has two competing consumers of limited GPU DRAM: static model weights (including quantized variants), transient activations (including continuous-batching accumulation), and the KV cache for long-running chat sessions. Sudden KV growth and tail-batching behaviour cause intermittent OOMs and tail latency spikes. Current slab/reserve heuristics are overly conservative for small tenants and too brittle under multi-tenant noise.

Goals: 1) Reduce observed OOM rate by at least 6x on P99 traffic under mixed chat/generation workloads. 2) Improve average token latency during high KV pressure by 10-20% through smarter headroom management. 3) Keep end-to-end cost neutral vs today by reclaiming unused reservations and enabling soft sharing where safe.

High-level approach: Implement a predictive headroom reservation system that maintains a small, dynamically-sized 'operational headroom' per GPU node and a per-tenant soft-budget for KV/activations. Key ideas:
- Sliding-window quantile prediction: use short-term (30s) and medium-term (5m) quantiles of KV growth and activation footprint to forecast 95th percentile peak requirements and set headroom accordingly.
- Soft reservations with preemption tiers: reserve minimal guaranteed bytes (hard) and a larger soft allocation that can be reclaimed under emergency by higher-priority workloads. This lets low-priority tenants use spare headroom without risking critical requests.
- Adaptive KV compaction/segmentation: allow KV cache to be compacted in-place (compress small tokens, coalesce expired keys) when headroom pressure is detected, and fall back to eviction policies prioritized by recency and token importance score.
- Spill-to-host fast-path: when reclaiming soft allocations is insufficient, spill cold KV segments or inactive activation slabs to pinned CPU memory with lightweight compression to free ephemeral GPU memory quickly and transparently.

Implementation plan: Phase 1 (measurement + sim): add instrumentation to collect per-request delta of weights+activations+kv, build a simulator to replay past traces and validate headroom policy parameters. Phase 2 (node agent + runtime hooks): ship node-level allocator changes that enforce hard vs soft quotas, KV compaction hooks, and spill-to-host. Phase 3 (gradual rollout + observability): enable policy behind feature flag for a small fraction of traffic, monitor regressions, enable auto-tuning of the prediction windows.

Trade-offs and risks: Prediction windows must balance responsiveness vs noise; overly aggressive reclamation can increase token latency due to compression/spill costs. Spill-to-host paths introduce CPU cost and possible cross-device bus contention. Need strong telemetry to detect regressions early and fast fallbacks to existing conservative allocator.
acceptance_criteria:
- Simulator replay on 10 representative traces shows OOM rate reduced by >= 6x and P99 token latency not worse than +10% in extreme cases.
- Node agent supports hard vs soft budget enforcement and can reclaim soft allocations within 50ms of pressure detection.
- KV compaction reduces KV footprint by at least 12% on average for tested long-chat traces.
- Feature flag rollout to 5% of capacity succeeds with no P1 incidents after 48h.
- Documentation describing configuration knobs and operator runbook merged to internal Confluence.
tasks: Add per-request memory delta telemetry to tracer and aggregate per-GPU time-series
Build replay simulator: ingest traces, apply headroom policy, emit metrics (OOMs, latency, reclaimed bytes)
Design node agent API for hard vs soft reservation enforcement (proto + RPC contract)
Implement KV compaction module with configurable compression levels and segment boundaries
Implement spill-to-host path with pinned CPU buffers and async restore path
Add billing/chargeback tag to soft allocation usage for accounting
Create dashboards: headroom-utilization, reclaimed-bytes, spill-events, p99-latency-by-tenant
Write operator runbook and rollback steps for rapid disable of feature flag
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Kaur: Initial proposal posted. Collected three week trace set (internal bucket 'runtime-traces/2026-02') covering chat-heavy, short-turn, and long-stream workloads.

2026-02-25 - Miguel Santos: Simulator skeleton implemented (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/842). Early runs show soft reservation reduces OOMs for a single-tenant replay but multi-tenant noise still causes spikes.
2026-03-02 - Design review notes from Priya Menon: prefer quantile hybrid (30s + 5m) vs single-window. Add safety cap that never reduces hard reservation below 8% of node DRAM for critical models.
2026-03-05 - Miguel Santos: KV compaction prototype reduces KV by ~14% on long-chat trace using fast LZ4 with chunking. Added microbench showing compression+decompress latency ~120us per chunk.
2026-03-08 - Security review (informal): spill-to-host path requires encryption-at-rest for pinned CPU buffers; added KMS integration task. Marking security_review_required=true for final sign-off.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Santos: Started node agent change branch (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/879). Added unit tests for hard vs soft enforcement and basic reclaim behavior. Planning 5% canary for 2026-03-22
